items.note: Framework paper with a small empirical study of professional designers on one poster brief examining how AI participation affects efficiency, creative exploration, and visual quality; the comparison condition and sample size are not stated and results are described as trend-level, so the full text must show whether a no-AI condition exists.

Within-subject online study varying the politeness strategy of AI email suggestions (one AI configuration versus another); the output outcome is whether writers mirror the suggested strategy, which is a convergence-toward-AI measure rather than a creativity score, so eligibility under criterion 3 is doubtful.

System paper with a within-subject study (N=12) comparing the TreeWriter hierarchical AI editor with Google Docs plus Gemini on long-document editing and creative writing; reported gains (idea exploration, AI helpfulness, perceived control) look self-reported, and N is far below 50.

Within-subject experiment in which 28 designers did conceptual design tasks with traditional sketching and with an image-generation tool, with design performance scored on novelty, variety, and fluency; N is below 50 and order randomization is not stated.

System paper on StarBurst (AI-generated remote associations for design ideation) with two user studies (N=32 and N=16) comparing it with a baseline system and with designers; claims more diverse and creative idea development, but whether ideas were rated or self-reported is unclear.

CHI system paper (PoemPalette) with a controlled experiment of 60 participants on Chinese poetry and haiku comparing the GenAI tool with AI and non-AI baselines on foundational understanding and creative outcomes; how creative outcomes are scored and whether assignment was random needs the full text.

Five-week quasi-experiment with Chinese design students comparing traditional and AI-assisted creation, with expert ratings of elaboration, fluency, flexibility, and originality plus self-reports; non-random design and sample size not stated.

Mechanical engineering design course study comparing student groups with and without ChatGPT-3.5 on concept generation (diversity of concepts, bias toward popular designs) and CAD modeling; assignment method and sample size not stated in the abstract.

Framework paper with a case study (Zaha Hadid style) in which design proposals made within the co-evolutionary human-AI framework were rated higher than prompt-engineering and style-model-adaptation baselines (AI configuration versus AI configuration); unclear whether separate participants were assigned to conditions and how many.

CHI system paper on an AI-assisted causal pathway diagram plugin for Miro, with a user study of 20 designers reporting lower workload and higher creativity during brainstorming; the comparison condition is implied but not stated, and creativity is likely self-reported (N below 50).
